statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so no current price path exists to score. Friday's verified close was inside its daily range with implied volatility lower, and Tail remains in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz reopening plan and a week of oil decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; rejected Hormuz plan and a 5.18% 10-year frame the 22:00Z reopen
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's cash close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. An inside-range close with declining implied volatility is a two-way auction, not the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures, which is why Tail sits at 6 despite a demanding macro backdrop. That backdrop is genuine and is carried in Stress at 55. The Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% at the 15-16 September meeting in a 12-0 vote, the first increase since 2023; the latest H.15 observation for 24 September shows the 10-year at 5.18%, the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47%; and Saturday reporting put the 10-year near 5.2%, its highest in roughly two decades, with market-implied odds of a further October increase around 66%. Equities absorbed that during the week, with the Nasdaq Composite up about 2% and the S&P 500 about 1.2%. One weekend development remains unpriced. WTI settled Friday at about $92.41, some 7.87% lower on the week, partly on optimism that the Strait of Hormuz might reopen; Trump then said on Saturday that he had rejected Iran's seven-day reopening proposal, while Brent held above $100. Because no venue is quoting, that information cannot be priced until CME Globex reopens at 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, which is the single flagged window in this publication and the penultimate hour of the forecast. Shared Finviz context collected at 23:12Z is explicitly delayed latest-session data and its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so it is used only as confirmation: Friday Technology rose 0.85%, Semiconductor Equipment & Materials 1.76%, six of eight megacaps were higher with MSFT up 3.66% and AAPL up 1.53% against META down 3.33% and TSLA down 1.54%, and six of seven tracked semiconductors were higher while INTC fell 3.45%. That internal rotation argues against index-level one-way structure. Confidence of 74 reflects verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and a full forward calendar set against price evidence that is now roughly 28 hours old.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours are the whole of Saturday 26 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Published Tail eased from 9 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 44 to 54 on the rate and Middle East backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 85 down to 75 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the penultimate slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore stays in the low band, easing to 5 through the dead hours and rising to 14 at the reopen before easing to 13, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz reopening plan, oil that shed 7.87% on the week, and a 10-year near a two-decade high meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Stress runs between 52 and 61 on that backdrop and Confidence troughs near 65 before improving as live price discovery resumes. The escalation condition would be an initial gap that extends with shallow or failed retracements and aligned cross-assets; an orderly two-way reopening auction would invalidate it.
